title: Tabs for peer sections
summary: Use tabs when a small set of peer sections share one context and users benefit from switching between them without navigating away.
problem: Tabs are often used for unrelated destinations or too many sections, creating hidden information and confusing keyboard behavior.
use_when: Sections are peers inside the same object or task context
Users are likely to compare or switch between sections repeatedly
avoid_when: Sections are steps in a required sequence
Each section deserves its own navigable destination or deep-linking model
rationale: They work best when switching is fast and the set is limited.

prefer_alternatives_if: The content should be visible simultaneously or the sections represent primary navigation
use_if: Sections are peers inside the same object or task context
Users are likely to compare or switch between sections repeatedly

requirements: Expose tablist, tab, and tabpanel relationships.
Selected state must be programmatically available.
Support documented keyboard movement between tabs.
keyboard: Use arrow-key behavior when implementing a true tablist composite.
Keep focus behavior consistent with activation strategy.

requirements: Keep tab labels short and mutually exclusive.
Preserve direct links to meaningful tab state when users need to share or return to it.
